# FDG9036

> DO NOT return a null `Task` or `Task<TResult>`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.2.5 Implementation Guidelines for Async Pattern Consistency.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9036
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Do not return a null task from '{0}'

FDG9036 reports a null or default literal, or a conditional access (x?.M()), returned as Task or Task<TResult> from a method, local function or property getter that is not async; in an async method such a value is the result, not the task. A null is seen directly, through a conversion, or in a branch of a conditional expression. Variables and fields that hold null, and lambdas, are not seen, so coverage is partial. ValueTask is a struct whose default value is a completed operation, so it is not checked. The body asks what the value means (an exception, or Task.CompletedTask or Task.FromResult), so there is no code fix; the fix changes no signature.

## From the book

Very few callers would ever check an Async method for a null `Task` being returned. Instead of returning null, consider what this value means and then choose a better alternative. For example, if an Async method cannot be started, it should throw an exception (see section 9.2.6.5). Alternatively, if the work is already done, return `Task.CompletedTask` or `Task.FromResult(result)`.
